label: rejected

evidence.V1: Top and three-quarter read clearly as a stone tile floor; front view and silhouette show a slab with a stepped row of raised tiles on top, still readable as flooring
evidence.V2: Big plinth and medium tiles in mixed sizes with three values are clear, but there is no small level at all (no cracks, chips, worn corners or grout detail)
evidence.V3: Stiff: every tile is a perfect rectangle at identical height on a rigid grid with uniform gaps; no stylised irregularity, tilt or rounding that flagstones usually get
evidence.V4: Tiles carry consistent soft chamfers that catch light (close_flagstones_studio), but the plinth's vertical corner and top edge are hard and unchamfered (close_edge_studio)
evidence.V5: Clean: no seams, pinches or z-fighting in studio or flat close-ups; 0 cross-shell overlaps, 0 flipped faces
evidence.V6: Disciplined: one stone grey in three values plus a darker plinth; sandstone/brick colourways keep the same structure, though the random light/dark tiles read slightly checkerboard-busy
evidence.V7: 476 tris vs module target 800 (ceiling 2000): under target
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, stone hue, chamfered tiles and T1 tiling (IoU ~0.98, cover ~0.99) fit the modular kit; minor mismatch from the unchamfered plinth
evidence.V9: Studio line correct for a modular piece: anchored, Box collision, CanTouch off, grid-corner pivot, Color white, SmoothPlastic

top_fixes: Break the rigid grid: slight per-tile height/tilt variation, softened or irregular corners, and a few chipped tiles so it reads as hand-laid flagstone
Chamfer the plinth edges (~0.05-0.07 studs) to match the tiles
Calm the value distribution (fewer darkest tiles, cluster values) so the surface reads less like a checkerboard
